entry_point.code: static inline const char* DecodeEntry(const char* p, const char* limit,

trace.code: non_shared and value_length are uint32_t varints read from the attacker-controlled block
the bounds check sums (*non_shared + *value_length) in uint32_t -> wraps; non_shared=1, value_length=0xffffffff -> sum=0 -> check passes
DecodeEntry returns p (accepts); Block::Iter::ParseNextKey builds value_ = Slice(p+non_shared, value_length) extending ~4 GiB past the buffer -> out-of-bounds read

preconditions: the attacker supplies or corrupts a leveldb table/block (e.g. an .ldb file, synced/imported database, or on-disk corruption)
the application iterates the block (normal read path)

evidence.vulnerable_version: google/leveldb <= 1.23 (latest release) and all commits before 29465588d3 (fix merged 2026-11-04, UNRELEASED)
evidence.fixed_version: unreleased (fix commit 29465588d3; latest tagged release 1.23 is still vulnerable)
evidence.observed_result: The REAL leveldb Block iterator (vendored upstream table/block.cc compiled vuln vs fixed) on the upstream test's crafted block: VULNERABLE accepts the entry (Valid=1), returns a value Slice of size 0xffffffff ending 4294967287 bytes past the 16-byte buffer, and reading it SIGSEGVs (out-of-bounds read confirmed). FIXED rejects it (Valid=0, status.IsCorruption=1).

real_exploit.target: google/leveldb table/block.cc DecodeEntry integer overflow -> out-of-bounds read
real_exploit.backend: real vendored upstream leveldb Block/DecodeEntry (fixed 29465588d3) vs the reverted vulnerable DecodeEntry, compiled with zig cc; crafted block = leveldb's own CorruptedBlockEntryLengthOverflow regression test input
real_exploit.demonstrated: a crafted leveldb block makes the vulnerable DecodeEntry pass its overflowing bounds check so the iterator over-reads ~4 GiB past the buffer (SIGSEGV); the fix rejects the entry as corruption
